entities.summary:
Nikolaus Gerbel was a German humanist, jurist, and doctor of both laws, who played a significant role in the development of Western legal thought during the late 16th century.

Born in the 1520s, Gerbel studied law in Erfurt and later became a prominent figure in the German humanist movement, influencing the legal and intellectual landscape of his time.

Gerbel's most notable contribution was his work on the concept of 'ius gentium,' which posits that natural law is universal and applies to all nations. This idea had a profound impact on the development of international law and the concept of human rights.

Despite his significant influence, Gerbel's legacy was largely overlooked until the 20th century, when scholars began to reevaluate his contributions to the history of Western legal thought.

Gerbel's work continues to be studied by scholars today, who seek to understand the complex interplay between law, culture, and politics in early modern Europe.

The Gerbel Collection, housed at the University of Erfurt, contains a vast array of manuscripts and documents related to Gerbel's life and work, providing a unique window into the intellectual and cultural landscape of 16th-century Germany.

In conclusion, Nikolaus Gerbel's contributions to the development of Western legal thought and his influence on the concept of human rights make him an important figure in the history of law and politics.

Gerbel's work serves as a testament to the enduring power of humanism and the importance of understanding the complex historical contexts in which legal and intellectual ideas emerge.

As we continue to grapple with the complexities of international law and human rights in the 21st century, Gerbel's work remains a vital and timely reminder of the importance of understanding the historical context in which these concepts emerged.
